name: SAINT LUCIA
lead: Saint Lucia is a volcanic island in the Caribbean. Two steep cones called the Pitons rise straight from the sea.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Saint Lucia sits between the Caribbean Sea and the Atlantic. The twin Pitons are a UNESCO World Heritage Site (a place the world protects). Gros Piton is 770 m tall and Petit Piton is 743 m.
Thick rainforest covers the inland, fed by 2,000 mm of rain a year. Sulphur Springs near Soufrière is the world's only drive-in volcano.
animals: The Saint Lucia Parrot, or Jacquot, is bright green with red, blue and yellow markings. It lives nowhere else.
Leatherback sea turtles, heavier than a motorbike, nest on the beaches each spring. Reefs shelter seahorses and flying fish.
culture: Saint Lucians blend French, African and British traditions. The Creole (mixed) language Kwéyòl sounds like French with a Caribbean twist. Its national day, Jounen Kwéyòl, comes every October.
Carnival bursts out each July with soca (lively dance music) and dazzling costumes. The national dish is green fig (unripe banana) and saltfish. Cricket is practically a religion.
history: Arawak, then Carib, people (the first islanders) lived here long before Europeans came. The harbour was a prize. Britain and France swapped control fourteen times between 1660 and 1814, a Caribbean record.
Enslaved Africans worked the sugar plantations (big farms). Their descendants form most of the population today. Slavery ended in 1834. Saint Lucia became fully independent on 22 February 1979.
wows: Saint Lucia has two Nobel Prize winners, more per person than any other country.
The Pitons are so famous that their shape alone shows Saint Lucia, even from space.
At Sulphur Springs, you can drive within 20 m of boiling volcanic mud, unique on Earth.
Saint Lucia Parrots grew from 150 birds in 1977 to over 1,000, thanks to local nature protectors.
Saint Lucia changed rulers 14 times, leaving French and British marks.
Bananas grown in its volcanic soil taste sweeter than most store-bought bananas.
The twin Pitons block the wind at Soufrière bay, giving some of the calmest sailing in the Caribbean.

myths.fact: A banana plant is a giant herb (a soft-stemmed plant) with no wood. Its trunk is tightly wrapped leaves.
The leatherback's shell is soft and leathery, with no hard plates.
